report:
We have a near-final plan, but it is not finished. A, B, and C accept most of the draft. B's latest reply raises three corrections, and I have not had a chance to check them with A and C.

I kept the shared list of needs, concerns, and expectations (NCEs). I named my own concerns, added them, checked them with each person, and invited disagreement. I changed the list when C and B disagreed. I disagreed with drafts that asked B to choose sides, put C behind A, used first-come-first-served alone, booked before pad access, or left open facts without review dates. I cannot make legal decisions or move money. No payment or ownership change is part of the plan.

The group has accepted a shared booking record, one block each before a second, at least two days' notice, full dates with a.m. or p.m. times, daytime pickup and return, pad access confirmation, who collects the trailer, return condition, damage notes, keys, and parking out of the way. A and C will compare purpose, deadline, date flexibility, length of use, and notice before the earlier pickup. In that same conversation, they will set the next firm block or pause only the disputed block. B will not choose. C corrected the list to say daytime pickup and return, not necessarily daytime use.

No exact dates, weekend choices, block length, joint check date, or review date are set. C needs the materials schedule for a home project in the next few weeks. A will share weekend candidates once C has that schedule and pad access is known. B will ask the landlord and report the answer, but cannot promise when. B's pad currently holds the trailer; that is not a promise that it will continue. B asks A and C to include insurance and registration papers in the joint check if applicable. I cannot determine legal requirements.

B does not agree that item five keeps her out of the middle. B read "me" in item five as a request for B to compare A and C's needs. I would rewrite item five with clear names: A and C pause only the disputed block or use another neutral process, I can compare needs against the list if they ask, and B does not compare the needs. I would send that correction and B's pad wording to A, B, and C for one more check. No firm booking should happen until B reports the landlord answer and says whether the pad is accessible.
